proposals.research_question: When does Ag capping thickness make a SERS band ratio unreliable as a proxy of molecular orientation?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: The selected population in near-field hot spots differs from the total adsorbed molecular population under capping-thickness interventions.
proposals.restricted_null: At fixed orientation distribution and mode response, orientation-only ratio is unchanged by capping thickness.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Conventional site-weighted Raman tensor plus electromagnetic excitation/Stokes enhancement allows the same result without new physics.
proposals.observable: Heldout vector of polarization-resolved band ratios R_kj(d).
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: The heldout prediction residual of orientation-only M0 increases when access-weighted local-field population differs from the bulk molecular orientation distribution; magnitude not yet fixed.
assumptions: Capping perturbation has measurable, independently constrained near-field profile
controls: near-field spectral response at excitation/Stokes wavelengths
proposals.intervention: Vary d, and where possible manipulate adsorption/coverage at fixed d.
proposals.heldout_test: Fit a restricted site-weighted model on subset of thickness d and test unfit polarization/mode vectors on withheld thicknesses.
proposals.local_falsifier: No out-of-sample benefit beyond independently characterized fixed orientation baseline in the predeclared thickness/coverage range disfavors this specified access-proxy model only.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: Access and field enhancement remain multiplicatively non-identifiable without an independent accessibility proxy.
proposals.development_value: Calibrates limits of an orientation band-ratio proxy within known SERS physics.

proposals.research_question: Can independently calibrated field-weighted orientation better predict Au/Ag SERS spectral shape than ensemble mean orientation?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: Mode responses are weighted by correlation of site occupancy, molecular orientation and local-field polarization.
proposals.restricted_null: Mean orientation and mean enhancement are sufficient predictors independent of hotspot occupancy distribution.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Weighted Raman-tensor ensemble with local field/chemistry contains this covariance by construction.
proposals.observable: Out-of-sample mode ratio spectra R_kj and prediction error between matched-complexity models.
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: An independently calibrated weighted-orientation model should reduce out-of-sample predictive loss relative to ensemble mean-only baseline only where occupancy–orientation correlations vary.
assumptions: Independent calibration of mediator to avoid using test SERS ratios
Equal effective model complexity in comparison
proposals.intervention: Perturb molecular coverage while mapping hotspot field distribution.
proposals.heldout_test: Hold out one Au/Ag wavelength and coverage combination, fitting latent mediator only on independent calibration data.
proposals.local_falsifier: No reproducible heldout gain under verified occupancy variation disfavors the specific predictor, not orientation-field coupling generally.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: Whether a genuinely SERS-independent site-specific mediator can be measured remains an experimental obstacle.
proposals.development_value: Quantifies confounding and tests usefulness of weighted ensemble orientation as a predictive proxy.

proposals.research_question: What independent perturbation separates access-to-field from optical enhancement and orientation?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: Adsorption-site occupancy is a separable mediator that changes the population contributing to enhanced Raman signals.
proposals.restricted_null: At fixed orientation and field, access perturbation makes no selective change to the contributing molecular population.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Established surface adsorption/site occupancy plus spatial field weighting predicts possible relative SERS ratio changes.
proposals.observable: Mode-resolved polarization band-ratio vector under matched field geometry and altered access.
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: Selectively moving accessible adsorbates between sites with nonproportional Raman response changes the band ratio; for proportional site spectra the ratio stays invariant.
assumptions: Independent measurement of site response ratios
Perturbation avoids morphology changes or directly characterizes changes
proposals.intervention: Modulate site occupancy at fixed nanostructure and verify substrate optical response.
proposals.heldout_test: Calibrate two-site ratios and occupancy on part of perturbation series, predict withheld access levels with fixed site spectra.
proposals.local_falsifier: Failure at fixed, independently measured occupancy and field parameters disproves this particular mixture parameterization only.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: Site-specific chemistry may change with occupancy; an independent access probe may still correlate with optical changes.
proposals.development_value: Builds a controlled decomposition study within established SERS mechanism.

proposals.research_question: Can the failure of an orientation-only SERS proxy be predicted quantitatively from an independently calibrated spectral-selectivity index?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: Spectrally selective excitation/Stokes near-fields and spatial hotspot sampling cause systematic departures from an orientation-only response model.
proposals.restricted_null: Once orientation distribution and geometry are held fixed, relative band ratios need no wavelength-selective weighting correction.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Standard frequency-resolved EM enhancement and tensor response already explain such corrections; this is quantitative regime calibration, not a new law.
independent_variables: dimensionless spectral-selectivity index χ from independent optical mapping
proposals.observable: Normalized prediction error on vector of polarization-resolved log band ratios.
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: Within a predeclared test domain, an EM-corrected model should outperform orientation-only M0 where independently estimated χ exceeds its uncertainty; nonmonotone behavior remains possible near resonances.
assumptions: Raman tensor orientation distribution separately characterized
Field spectra calibrated without fitting test band ratio
controls: independent near-field excitation and Stokes transfer function
proposals.intervention: Vary λ and capping thickness while holding or tracking orientation/chemistry.
proposals.heldout_test: Fit model and error tolerance on training λ,d; freeze χ and response parameters, test new λ,d combinations with predictive uncertainty bands.
proposals.local_falsifier: Predeclared χ-dependent accuracy trend does not hold on out-of-sample λ,d within matched chemistry and orientation; rejects only that calibration claim.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: No universal transition threshold or new physics is implied by a smooth predictive crossover.
proposals.development_value: Develops a falsifiable quantitative map of the reliability domain of orientation proxies.

proposals.research_question: Does independently measured SERS-active orientation distribution improve prediction over bulk ensemble orientation?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: Hotspot-dependent weighting makes SERS-active molecular orientation distribution differ from ensemble-average distribution.
proposals.restricted_null: Ensemble orientation adequately represents the distribution of molecules contributing to SERS.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Conventional weighted Raman tensor/site ensemble naturally creates a difference between unweighted and enhanced signal populations.
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: A separately calibrated SERS-active orientation distribution improves heldout ratio prediction where local-field orientation/site covariance is appreciable.
assumptions: Hotspot-sensitive orientation measurement does not reuse target SERS ratios
controls: bulk orientation distribution independent of SERS
proposals.intervention: Vary optical hotspot spatial structure while tracking adsorption.
proposals.heldout_test: Estimate hotspot-weighted population on independent structural measurements and predict unseen excitation and polarization ratios.
proposals.local_falsifier: No prospective predictive gain from independently measured weighted orientation over bulk distribution in the specified matched regime disfavors this proxy only.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: The independent hotspot orientation assay may not be practically feasible; inversion from SERS would be circular.
proposals.development_value: Calibrates when bulk orientation measurements are misleading for near-field spectroscopy.

proposals.research_question: At fixed stationary site occupancy, how does exchange-rate scaling affect time-window SERS statistics?
proposals.mechanistic_hypothesis: Site exchange kinetics alter temporal covariance even when stationary pooled mean intensities remain unchanged.
proposals.restricted_null: Stationary 2-state CTMC with rates α,β, emissions A_k,s, and fixed π; scaling both rates c preserves pooled mean but changes covariance decay.
proposals.known_physics_envelope: Known Markov spectral diffusion/adsorption kinetics predict rate-dependent correlation and finite-window variance; novelty requires residual effect beyond a calibrated kinetics null.
independent_variables: exchange relaxation rate λ=α+β measured independently
proposals.observable: Intensity autocovariance C_kl(u), finite-window variance Var(Ibar_k,T), pooled band ratio and per-window ratio distribution kept distinct.
proposals.quantitative_or_ordinal_prediction: For stationary two-state CTMC, C_kl(u)=π1π2 ΔA_kΔA_l exp(-λ|u|) and Var(Ibar_k,T)=2σ²[Tτ−τ²(1−exp(−T/τ))]/T² with τ=1/λ; pooled mean ratio is unchanged under common rate scaling.
assumptions: State-specific emissions and π are fixed under kinetic perturbation
controls: shot noise and detector response removal
proposals.intervention: Change exchange kinetics at fixed π using independently verified perturbation; measure multiple T.
proposals.heldout_test: Estimate α,β and emission amplitudes on training trajectories and independently; freeze and predict withheld window lengths and cross-band covariance.
proposals.local_falsifier: Observed cross-band covariance vs T outside preregistered uncertainty after rate and detector calibration disfavors this fixed-parameter 2-state Markov model, not exchange in general.
proposals.surviving_uncertainty: Per-window ratio mean may change even when pooled ratio does not; complex multistate memory can violate the two-state null.
proposals.development_value: Identifies a tractable, quantitative temporal measurement program within known stochastic SERS physics.

provenance: Analyst-designed development seeds, NOT model output or empirical discovery
